classification.difficultyReason: Factor the expression inside the absolute value and handle the zero factor separately before division.

answer.short:
$2\le x\le4$.

Check $x=2$ separately, then divide by $|x-2|$ for $x\ne2$.
answer.worked:
Factor the left-hand side:
$$|(x-2)(x-3)|\le|x-2|.$$
When $x=2$, both sides are zero, so the inequality holds. For $x\ne2$, divide by the positive number $|x-2|$:
$$\begin{align*}|x-3|&\le1\\-1&\le x-3\le1\\2&\le x\le4\end{align*}$$
Including the separately checked value $x=2$, the solution is $2\le x\le4$.
